analysis_notes.gap_analysis: The source text introduces several key concepts — בֵּין הַמִּצְווֹת (the sacred space between mitzvot), מִצְוָה (commandment), זְרִיזוּת (alacrity/rushing), צַדִּיק (the righteous one who progresses level-by-level), בַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה (the penitent who must leap to holiness), קְדֻשָּׁה (holiness), and מִדַּרְגָּא לְדַרְגָּא (from level to level) — none of which appear in bechina-typed edges for this Torah (there are none). The two dataset edges that do exist for reference 1059 ('cause' and 'eitza' typed) connect מצוה and בין המצוות in a directional/causal relationship, which is consistent with the text's argument: the mitzvah draws (גּוֹרֶרֶת) the next mitzvah via the in-between dimension. No bechina equating language ('הוּא בְּחִינַת', 'נִקְרָא', 'כַּנַּ"ל' used as an equation) appears anywhere in the source text. The Rebbe uses the word 'בְּחִינָה' many times but only as a noun designating a 'level' or 'dimension' — not as the symmetric equivalence connective that would generate bechina edges. The conceptual relationships in the text are entirely causal: rushing CAUSES loss of the in-between dimension; slowing down ENABLES capturing it; for the ba'al teshuva there IS no in-between dimension so rushing ENABLES reaching holiness. This causal structure precludes bechina package formation. No additions to packages can be proposed because there are no packages and no bechina formulations in the source text to anchor any proposed addition.
